*Updated 2026-10-05 · 113 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and thirteen works. The October 5 piece scores 1, pulling the last twelve to 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1 — median 2, ceiling still 3, and the last four scores read 1, 1, 2, 1. That is not a plateau anymore; it is a slide. No 4 since late July means fifteen weeks without one, and the two recent 3s now sit isolated inside a deteriorating tail rather than anchoring a stable band.

Camera position has not moved in over a month. Straight-on sits at 27 of 113 all-time, overhead at 12, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show only 2 overhead and nothing else off-axis. The September 7 hoofprint piece and the September 25 barometer piece each scored 3 through scale violation, and that mechanism has now been used at least twice consecutively without producing a 4. A third pull from the same lever will produce another 1 or 2. The next displacement needs to come from camera axis: directly overhead flattening the focal object into a diagram, or low enough that the object becomes ceiling and the viewer becomes floor. Both of those positions are underrepresented at 12 and 4 respectively, and neither has appeared in the last twelve.

Figure count is the other stalled variable. The last twelve show two frames with one figure and two with none; no frame carries two or more. The archive's 4-scored works — Ceuta, Pakistan, Venezuela, Japan — each depended on something going wrong between bodies or between a body and the frame. A zero-figure composition can score 3 when the accident is strong enough, but it cannot reliably score 4. A second figure placed incorrectly — wrong posture, wrong gaze, wrong scale relative to the first — still outperforms any secondary accident on a figureless frame.

Registers are consolidating dangerously. Aftermath and menace together account for 44 of 113 all-time and have dominated the recent window with no reprieve, no reckoning, and no encroachment appearing at all in the last twelve. Those three should return only when the anchor makes them unavoidable, not as variety for its own sake, but their absence has narrowed the emotional range of the recent work in a way the scores reflect.

Move the camera axis, introduce a second figure doing something wrong, and do both before the current slide becomes the new mean.
